docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Help build Lucky and Pozzo. Start with the development setup, then read the architecture notes before changing internals.

  • Development setup - Clone, configure, and build the repository.
  • Testing - Run the test suite and add coverage for your changes.
  • Engine architecture - How the runtime is layered and where to add code.
  • Editor architecture - How the editor is structured and how it talks to the engine.
  • Adding components and systems - Extend the ECS without breaking existing scenes.
  • Adding editor features - Add a panel, command, or inspector field.
  • Style and review - Formatting, naming, and the pull-request checklist.

docs.title: Add a component
docs.text:
1. Define the struct in Engine/include/Components/.
  2. Register it in a plugin: registry.RegisterComponent<T>().
  3. Add reflection in Engine/include/Reflection/ComponentReflect.hpp if it should serialize.
  4. Add an IPluginEditor if it needs custom inspector widgets.
  5. Add a Lua binding if scripts need to touch it.

docs.title: Add a system
docs.text:
1. Define the class in Engine/include/Systems/ and Engine/src/Systems/.
  2. Register it in a plugin: registry.RegisterSystem<T>().
  3. Document ordering constraints: register dependencies first.

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep components dumb and small.
  • One system, one job.
  • Queue destruction; never mutate a container you are iterating.
  • Prefer several small components over one large one.
  • Bundle registration in a plugin.

docs.text:

  3. Add it to the default dock layout if needed.

docs.text: Implement IPluginEditor and register it in InspectorPanel::InspectorPanel().

docs.title: Add a menu item
docs.text: Add to EditorLayer::DrawSceneMenuItems() or the relevant menu builder. Keep shortcuts consistent with the existing Ctrl+S / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V scheme.

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
• The editor only writes component data; systems do the work.
  • Clamp values early in inspector widgets.
  • Keep serialization in sync.
  • Use asset pickers for paths.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• EditorLayer owns the panels and the dockspace, and bridges the engine's onUI and customRender callbacks.
  • Panels implement IEditorPanel and read/write the same Registry.
  • EditorConfig extends SceneConfig with editor-only state (selected asset, requested scene, script font size).
  • Gallery manages projects.json and project creation.
  • Scaffold generates project, system, and plugin files.

docs.title: Editor vs. game
docs.text:
The editor creates a normal Engine::Application with an EditorMode resource. ScriptSystem checks for that resource and stays idle, so scripts only run in the game process. The multiplayer plugin is not loaded into the editor process.

The editor edits a live registry and serializes it to .scene; the game deserializes the same file and runs it.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
• Core: Application, Registry, VirtualResolution, rendering, logging, errors.
  • ECS: entities, components, systems, resources.
  • Plugins: bundles of components, systems, and resources behind one Init().
  • Assets: AssetManager, bundler, project paths.
  • Scripting: ScriptComponent, ScriptSystem, Lua API.
  • Networking: replication and multiplayer plugins on top of ENet.
  • Serialization: scene and prefab files (separate module).

docs.title: Where to add code
docs.text:
• New data: a component struct in Engine/include/Components.
  • New behaviour: a system in Engine/include/Systems and Engine/src/Systems.
  • New feature: a plugin in Engine/include/Plugins and Engine/src/Plugins.
  • New Lua binding: a module under Engine/include/Scripting/LuaAPI.

Register components and systems in a plugin rather than in main(). Keep main() to plugin instantiation and entity spawning.

docs.title: Ordering constraints
docs.text:
• HierarchyPlugin before PositionPlugin.
  • ReplicationPlugin before MultiplayerPlugin.
  • Systems register in dependency order; registration order is update order.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text:
Build scenes and games in Lucky, the visual editor that sits on top of the engine.

  • Gallery - A look at the editor and the projects it ships with.
  • Interface - Hierarchy, Scene View, Inspector, and the other panels.
  • Entities - Create, select, and organize entities.
  • Prefabs - Reusable entity templates and instances.
  • Scenes - Save, load, and structure scene files.
  • Input mapping - Bind actions and axes for play mode.
  • Play mode - Run, pause, and inspect a scene while editing.
  • Multiplayer - Preview and test networked scenes.
  • Command line - Open projects and automate the editor from a terminal.
  • Shipping a game - Package an editor-made game for players.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: RTypeEditor can create a project, a system, or a plugin from the terminal. The same functions live in Editor::CreateProject, Editor::CreateSystem, and Editor::CreatePlugin. With no arguments, the Gallery opens as usual.

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
./RTypeEditor new <name> [--path <dir>] [--description <text>]

<name> is the window title. --path is the project directory; when omitted it is ./<name> in the current working directory. --description is stored in the Gallery list.

The command writes test.scene, project.json, assets/, and input.json. It also adds the project to the Gallery list and opens the editor on test.scene. The Gallery window is not shown.

The scene uses the project's name as its title, a 1280×720 window, 60 FPS, and a build executable name equal to the project name with spaces removed. main.cpp is not written; the editor generates it when you build.

If test.scene already exists, the command prints an error and does not open the editor. A project path already in the Gallery list is not added again.

docs.title: Create a system
docs.text:
./RTypeEditor create system <Name> [--path <dir>]

<Name> is a C++ identifier. System is appended when the name does not already end with it, so Damage and DamageSystem both create DamageSystem.

--path is where the files are written; when omitted it is the current working directory. The command walks upward to find Engine/CMakeLists.txt (or an engine tree in the current folder) and updates that CMake so the new sources build.

  • Inside the engine: include/Systems/<Name>System.hpp, src/Systems/<Name>System.cpp, and entries appended to Engine/CMakeLists.txt.
  • Inside a Gallery project: system/<Name>System.hpp, system/<Name>System.cpp, plus system/build.cmake and system/rtype_scaffold_register.hpp for editor builds.

Rebuild after scaffolding. Existing files are left unchanged.

docs.title: Create a plugin
docs.text:
./RTypeEditor create plugin <Name> [--path <dir>]

<Name> is a C++ identifier. Plugin is appended when the name does not already end with it. --path works the same as for create system.

In the engine tree, Health and HealthPlugin both create the usual include/ and src/ layout under Engine/. In a Gallery project they are created under system/ instead, with the same CMake and registration hooks as project systems.

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: A missing name, an unknown command, or an existing file prints an [ERROR] line and returns 1. Success prints an [INFO] line and returns 0. create returns after writing the files. new returns when the editor window closes.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: An entity is a numeric id. It has no data of its own; components attached to it give it behaviour and appearance.

docs.title: Creating
docs.text:
• Right-click empty space in the Hierarchy and choose Create Empty Entity.
  • Entities created from code use registry.CreateEntity(), which attaches a default Position and Rotation.

Every entity the editor creates gets a Name component so it can be displayed.

docs.title: Selecting and editing
docs.text: Click an entity in the Hierarchy or in the Scene view to select it. The Inspector then shows its components. Drag values to change them; changes apply immediately and are written to the registry.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
Drag a row onto another row to parent it; drop on empty space to detach. Parent motion is propagated by HierarchySystem before PositionSystem snapshots previous positions, so children follow their parents without drift.

Destroying a parent destroys its descendants. Parent::relative = true makes a child follow the parent's delta rather than copying its absolute transform.

docs.title: Copy, paste, and delete
docs.text:
• Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V (Hierarchy focused) copies and pastes the selected subtree.
  • Right-click a row for the same actions.
  • Del removes the selected entity and its descendants.

Pasted entities keep the original parent and position, so they overlap until you move them. Names are deduplicated.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: The Name component is what the editor displays. Entities without one fall back to their id. Rename from the Inspector or by double-clicking the row in the Hierarchy.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: The Gallery is the first screen you see when you launch RTypeEditor with no arguments. It lists your projects and lets you create new ones.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text: Each project card displays the project name, description, path, and last-opened date. Click a card to open the project's startup scene in the editor. Projects are stored in projects.json under your configuration directory.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
Click + New Project and fill in the dialog:

Field Meaning Name Window title and project identity Description Optional text shown on the card Path Project folder; use Browse... to pick it

A project folder contains test.scene, project.json, assets/, and input.json. main.cpp is generated when you build.

docs.title: Opening a scene directly
docs.text:
./build/RTypeEditor path/to/test.scene

This skips the Gallery and opens the scene. The project folder is the scene's parent.

docs.title: Removing a project
docs.text: Projects can be removed from the list from the card's options menu. Removing a project from the Gallery does not delete its files.

docs.title: Input mapping
docs.text: The Input Map panel edits the actions and keybinds stored in input.json. Actions are string names that gameplay reads through Controller::isActionActive.

docs.title: Using the panel
docs.text:
1. Open Input Map from the menu bar or its tab.
  2. Type an action name and click + Add Action.
  3. Expand the action, click + Add Keybind, then click the Key button and press the desired key.

Action names are case-sensitive: left, Left, and LEFT are three different actions.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: The map is stored in the scene as m_InputMap and baked into the game launcher at build time. Changing it requires a rebuild before the game sees the new bindings.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text: The editor is a dockable ImGui workspace. Every panel reads and writes the same Engine::Registry; there is no separate editor scene format until you save.

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
Panel Purpose Hierarchy Entity tree, selection, copy/paste, prefab drops Inspector Component editors for the selected entity Scene The game rendered at virtual resolution through the engine camera Assets Project asset browser; drag images and prefabs into the scene Preview Selected image or prefab preview; edits shared prefab data Connections Signal subscriptions between entities Console Engine logs, errors, and build output Input Map Actions and keybinds stored in input.json State State resources, initial state, and live activation Settings Project settings, build, and multiplayer launch Script Editor Lua source editing with syntax highlighting

Drag tabs to rearrange. The dock layout is stored in imgui.ini next to the executable.

docs.title: Scene view
docs.text:
The scene view is not an approximation: it renders the registry with the same systems and camera the game uses, at the project's virtual resolution. Resize the window and the canvas letterboxes exactly as it will in the game.

  • Click an entity to select it.
  • Drag the centre handle to move it; drag the X, Y, or rotation handles to constrain.
  • Right- or middle-drag to pan the editor camera.
  • Scroll to zoom the editor view (this does not change the game camera).

Runtime-only behaviour (Lua, multiplayer) is not simulated here; use Play.

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
The tree shows parent/child relationships. Entities without a Parent are roots.

  • Right-click empty space to spawn an entity.
  • Right-click a row for copy, paste, rename, delete, and prefab actions.
  • Drag a row onto another row to parent it; drop on empty space to detach.
  • Delete removes the selected entity and its descendants.

A Name component is what the editor displays. Entities without one fall back to their id.

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text:
The inspector shows one collapsible section per component on the selected entity.

  • Drag a value to change it; changes apply immediately.
  • Right-click empty space to add a component from the registered list.
  • Right-click a component header to remove or reset it.
  • Components without a dedicated editor plugin still appear with a generic field editor.

Edits are written directly into component memory. Save before large changes.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
The assets panel browses the project's assets/ directory.

  • Double-click an image to preview it.
  • Drag an image onto an entity in the Hierarchy or Scene view to assign a sprite.
  • Drag a Hierarchy row onto the panel to write a .prefab.
  • Drag a .prefab back to instantiate it.

The path stored in components is project-relative, so the same scene works from the editor and from the built game.

docs.title: Copy, paste, and prefabs
docs.text:
Right-click a Hierarchy row, or press Ctrl+C while the Hierarchy is focused, to copy an entity and its children. Ctrl+V creates a new subtree with the same data.

A pasted entity keeps the original parent and position, so it overlaps the original until you move it. Names are deduplicated: enemy1 becomes enemy1(1), then enemy1(2). The same numbering applies to instantiated prefabs.

Dragging a row to Assets writes <Name>.prefab in the folder you are viewing. If the name exists, the next file is Name_2.prefab, then Name_3.prefab.

Selecting a .prefab in Assets opens it in Preview. Changing the sprite path, scale, shape size, or script there updates every instance. Positions stay where each instance was placed.

docs.title: Console
docs.text: Engine logs are buffered and shown here with severity colouring. Build output from Play also lands in the Console, which is the first place to look when a launch fails.

docs.title: Settings and Play
docs.text:
Project settings cover the window, virtual resolution, target FPS, and build target. The Play buttons launch the real binaries:

  • Build (hammer) compiles the project.
  • Play - one game process with the current scene.
  • Play Multiplayer - one server plus N clients, each in its own window.
  • Stop - closes every process started by the current Play session.

See Play mode and Multiplayer.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text:
Preview and test networked scenes.

In plain words: the editor is the drawing board. When you hit Play Multiplayer, it starts a referee (the server) and a few players (the clients) as separate windows, all looking at the same drawing. You close them all with Stop.

For what happens inside those processes, read the Engine → Networking page. This page is only about using the feature.

docs.title: 1. Where it lives
docs.text:
Two places in the editor:

Control Location What it does Play Multiplayer (people icon) / Stop main toolbar, right of the single-player Play button launches / kills the whole playtest Client Count Settings panel → Multiplayer Playtest how many client windows to launch (1–5) Headless Server Settings panel → Multiplayer Playtest run the server with no window

The toolbar buttons, left to right:

[ Build ]   [ Play ]   [ Play Multiplayer ]   (or)   [ Stop ]
  • Play launches a single, single-player process.
  • Play Multiplayer launches 1 server + N clients.
  • Stop (replaces the play buttons while games run) kills every launched process.

docs.title: 2. The settings
docs.text:
Settings panel → Multiplayer Playtest:

Setting Range Meaning Client Count 1–5 how many client processes to launch; clamped to PlayerSlotState::kMaxPlayers Headless Server on/off adds --headless to the server, so it runs without a window

The count is capped at 5 because the engine assigns one distinct color slot per connected player (0–4). The transport also enforces it, so a sixth client is simply refused. Player N gets color slot N-1; in the shipped R-Type project that maps to sprite block 5N-4 .. 5N.

The server address and port are not exposed here yet - a launched client always connects to 127.0.0.1:3000 (see §8).

This will be modified to allow flexibility

docs.title: 3. The Network component in the Inspector
docs.text:
Select an entity (or select a .prefab in the Assets panel) and the Inspector shows a Network section when the entity has a NetworkComponent. Add it from the component menu like any other.

Field Control Meaning Authority dropdown: Server / Client / Shared who simulates the entity (see below) Sync Transform checkbox replicate Position + Rotation every tick Sync Sprite checkbox replicate the sprite (path, offset, scale, flips) Prefab Path text field + drag-and-drop target prefab to instantiate on the other machine when spawning Network ID read-only label engine-assigned; shows (assigned on connect) until then

You can type a prefab path or drag a .prefab from the Assets panel straight onto the field.

docs.title: Choosing an authority
docs.text:
Authority Means Use it for Server the server simulates it; clients follow enemies, pickups, moving platforms, hazards Client one client sends input; the server simulates it each connected player Shared not synced at all; built identically from the scene walls, floors, background

A Client entity in the scene is a template: the server destroys it on startup and spawns one copy per connected player from Prefab Path. So you author the player once, set the prefab path, and every connection gets its own instance - with its own color slot.

docs.title: 4. What the button actually launches
docs.text:
When you click Play Multiplayer with a scene open and a client count of 3, the editor spawns:

Game --server <scene> [--headless]     # the server
Game --client <scene>                  # client 1
Game --client <scene>                  # client 2
Game --client <scene>                  # client 3

Each process is started in its own process group so Stop can kill the whole tree without touching the editor. On Windows the same happens through CreateProcessA / TerminateProcess.

The processes themselves parse these flags in MultiplayerPlugin::Init (see the engine page); --headless additionally disables the window and rendering.

docs.title: 5. Quick start: a multiplayer scene in five minutes
docs.text:
This is the minimal recipe. It assumes one player prefab and one enemy.

1. Author the player as a prefab.

  • Build the entity in the scene: Position, SpriteComponent, a collider, and whatever script drives it (player.lua).
  • Drag it into the Assets panel to write Player.prefab.

2. Make it networked.

  • Select Player.prefab (or the entity) and add a Network component.
  • Set Authority → Client, tick Sync Transform and Sync Sprite.
  • Set Prefab Path → Prefabs/Player.prefab (drag the prefab in).

3. Place the template in the scene.

  • Keep one instance of the player in the scene. It is only a template; the server will replace it with one live player per connection. Don't script it to depend on being "The Player".

4. Author the enemy.

  • Add a Network component to the enemy (or its prefab) with Authority → Server, Sync Transform on. Because it exists in the scene on every machine, it needs no prefab path.

5. Build, then play.

  • Click 🔨 Build (Play Multiplayer does not build for you - see §8).
  • Set Client Count to 2 in Settings.
  • Click 👥 Play Multiplayer. Two client windows appear and connect; the tail of the server log shows the clients connecting.
  • Click ⏹ Stop when done.

Your game code stays ordinary: player.lua reads Net.input(entity), moves, shoots; the engine handles the rest. In single-player the same script falls back to the local controller (Net.isNetworked() is false).

docs.title: 6. How flexible is it? Examples
docs.text: The mechanism is genre-agnostic: you are only choosing, per entity, who owns it and what gets synchronised. Below are sketches for very different kinds of games, all using the same editor controls.

docs.title: a. Side-scrolling shooter (the shipped R-Type example)
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Player Client transform + sprite one per connection, distinct color slot Enemy Server transform (+ sprite if it animates) exists in the scene on both sides Bullet / explosion Server transform + sprite created at runtime, marked with Net.replicate Walls / background Shared - identical everywhere, zero bandwidth 
-- playerGun.lua: fire and let the engine replicate the bullet
local bullet = Entity.create()
Transform.setPosition(bullet, x, y)
Net.replicate(bullet, "Server", true, true)

docs.title: b. Top-down arena brawler / party game
docs.text:
Same shape as (a) but with free 2D movement and pickups:

Entity Authority Sync Notes Player Client transform + sprite each client controls its own Pickup Server transform + sprite server decides who grabs it Arena tiles Shared - level geometry

Because the server owns the pickup, two players reaching it on the same frame resolves deterministically - no client gets to "win" by touching first locally.

docs.title: c. Co-op action / physics playground
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Player Client transform Crate / ball / lever Server transform shared physics the server resolves Door Server sprite opened by an RPC when the lever is pulled

Use Net.rpc for discrete interactions ("open the door"), and Server authority for anything both players must agree on.

-- on the lever, server side
Net.rpc(leverEntity, "doorOpened", { id = self.doorId })

docs.title: d. Turn-based board / card game
docs.text:
Turn-based games barely need state streaming at all - they need events:

  • Add a Network component with Authority → Client to each player's hand/avatar, or skip replication entirely and use RPCs.
  • Turn actions are Net.rpc(entity, ...) calls (playCard, endTurn), and the server validates them and broadcasts the resulting state.
  • Because a snapshot is sent every tick regardless, you can also just mark the board Server and let the state replicate; no interpolation issues when nothing moves.

docs.title: e. Racing / sports with several local players
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Car / athlete Client transform Track decorations Shared - Checkpoints / finish line Server - (triggers, resolved server-side)

The server decides finishing order and lap counts; clients only ever report steering and throttle.

docs.title: f. Single-player still works
docs.text: A scene with Network components still runs if launched without any network flag (the ordinary ▶ Play button, or Game with no arguments). No host is created and Net.isNetworked() is false, so scripts take their single-player branch. You do not maintain two versions of a game.

docs.title: Summary table
docs.text: Genre Who is Client-authority Who is Server-authority Discrete events Shooter players enemies, bullets shoot Arena brawler players pickups, hazards grab Co-op action players physics objects interact Turn-based (optional) hands board, deck play/end turn Racing vehicles checkpoints lap Solitaire-like - - all RPC

docs.title: 7. Recipes for different genres
docs.text:
Deeper than the sketches above: for each genre, what to tag in the Inspector and the Lua pattern that makes it work. Every recipe is editor + Lua only - no C++.

Two facts shape all of them. Only Position (+ Rotation.angle) and the sprite replicate declaratively; anything else (health, money, turn, cards) travels as an RPC, or is encoded in a sprite path. And a Lua script cannot instantiate a .prefab - it builds bare entities with Entity.create() + Component.add*. The workaround: build on the server, then hand a prefabPath to Net.replicate(...) so clients still instantiate the authored prefab (see the engine TODO).

Two blocks reused everywhere:

-- true in single-player and on the server; false on a client
local function shouldSimulate()
    if not Net.isNetworked() then return true end
    return Net.isServer()
end

-- Server: create a runtime object; clients instantiate the authored prefab
local e = Entity.create()
Transform.setPosition(e, x, y)
Component.addSprite(e, "assets/thing.png", 0, 0, 2, 2)
Component.addBoxCollider(e, 24, 24)
Net.replicate(e, "Server", true, true, "Prefabs/Thing.prefab")

docs.title: 7.1 Pong / air-hockey  -  real-time, almost no state
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Ball (scene) Server Transform the server moves it in Lua Paddle prefab Client Transform one per connection (slots 0, 1) Goal / wall Shared - identical everywhere

Paddle (server side):

function Paddle:onUpdate(e, dt)
    if not shouldSimulate(e) then return end
    local i = Net.input(e) or { UP = Controller.isActionActive("UP"),
                                DOWN = Controller.isActionActive("DOWN") }
    local dy = (i.DOWN and 1 or 0) - (i.UP and 1 or 0)
    Transform.translate(e, 0, dy * SPEED * dt)
end

The ball needs no networking code at all - it is Server authority, so syncTransform carries it to both clients. Score is the only extra state: Net.broadcast("score", { l = .., r = .. }) on the server, Net.on("score", ...) on clients.

Why it fits: the simplest proof that a moving object "just appears" on every screen.

docs.title: 7.2 Top-down arena shooter  -  bullets, health, respawn
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Player prefab Client Transform + Sprite color from slot Bullet (runtime) Server Transform + Sprite server builds it; clients get the prefab Wall Shared -

Firing uses the Net.replicate(..., prefabPath) pattern. Health is not synced, so the server announces it:

-- server, on hit
Net.rpc(victim, "hurt", { hp = newHp })
-- client handler
Net.onEntityRpc("hurt", function(e, data) self.hp = data.hp; self.flash = 0.2 end)

player_input carries the whole set of active action names marked networked, so extra actions (dash / reload) work on the server too - no extra RPC needed as long as the keybind is networked:

if Net.isServer() and input.DASH then Net.rpc(e, "dash", {}) end

Respawn should reuse the player entity rather than destroy and re-create it: the server binds a player's identity and color slot when it spawns them, and a plain Entity.destroy from a script does not release that binding or the slot (only a disconnect does, or an explicit Net.untrack). So reset in place:

Transform.setPosition(e, spawnX, spawnY)
Component.setColliderEnabled(e, false)
Component.setOpacity(e, 0)

Why it fits: a twitch shooter with health, respawn and score, from just Net.replicate + Net.rpc.

docs.title: 7.3 Co-op platformer  -  a server-driven world
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Player prefab Client Transform + Sprite Platform prefab Server Transform the server animates it in Lua Lever / Door Server Sprite sprite swaps on/off; the door slides via a broadcast Terrain Shared -

Continuous state - the server animates, clients just watch:

function Platform:onUpdate(e, dt)
    if not shouldSimulate(e) then return end
    self.t = (self.t or 0) + dt
    Transform.setPosition(e, self.x0, self.y0 + math.sin(self.t) * 60)
end

Discrete event - a lever is an RPC, not a stream:

-- lever, server
Component.setSpritePath(e, self.on and ON_IMG or OFF_IMG)
Net.broadcast("door", { open = self.on })

Why it fits: the two flavours side by side - replicate a transform (continuous) vs. announce an event (discrete).

docs.title: 7.4 Turn-based card / board game  -  RPCs and sprites
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Seat prefab (invisible) Client none gives each client an identity + slot CardSlot × N Server Sprite the sprite path is the card HUD none - local text per client

Encode categorical state in the sprite path and let Sync Sprite do the work:

-- server, when a card is revealed
Component.setSpritePath(cardSlot, "cards/ace_spades.png")  -- clients update automatically

Moves are RPCs, validated on the server (which owns the rules in a script's self):

Net.rpc(seat, "playCard", { slot = 3 })                   -- client intent
Net.onEntityRpc("playCard", function(seat, data)           -- server authority
    if self.turnSlot ~= Net.playerSlot(seat) then return end
    -- ... validate the card ...
    self.turnSlot = (self.turnSlot + 1) % Net.maxPlayers()
    Net.broadcast("turn", { slot = self.turnSlot })
end)

Why it fits: nothing moves, so there is no tick, no interpolation and no cheating surface; the server is simply the only rule-keeper.

docs.title: 7.5 Co-op horde / tower-defense  -  many server units + an economy
docs.text:
Entity Authority Sync Notes Player prefab Client Transform + Sprite Director (empty + script) none - the server spawns waves Zombie (runtime) Server Transform + Sprite Net.replicate(..., "Prefabs/Zombie.prefab") Tower (runtime) Server Transform placed via RPC Path / terrain Shared -

The server director spawns a wave:

for i = 1, waveSize do
    local z = Entity.create()
    Transform.setPosition(z, spawnX, spawnY + i * 40)
    Component.addSprite(z, "assets/zombie.png", 0, 0, 3, 3)
    Component.addBoxCollider(z, 40, 40)
    Component.addScript(z, "scripts/zombie.lua")
    Net.replicate(z, "Server", true, true, "Prefabs/Zombie.prefab")
end

Building goes client → server → everyone:

Net.rpc(seat, "build", { x = mx, y = my, kind = "gun" })   -- client
Net.onEntityRpc("build", function(seat, d)                  -- server validates + spends
    if self.money < COST then return end
    self.money = self.money - COST
    local t = Entity.create()
    -- ... place + dress the tower ...
    Net.replicate(t, "Server", true, false, "Prefabs/Tower.prefab")
    Net.broadcast("money", { v = self.money })
end)

Why it fits: 5 humans, dozens of replicated AI and a shared economy, from two verbs (Net.replicate, Net.broadcast).

docs.title: 7.6 The palette, at a glance
docs.text: You need… Editor / Lua A thing everyone sees move NetworkComponent Server + Sync Transform One entity per player NetworkComponent Client + Prefab Path (scene template) Something that never changes Shared A bullet / effect made at runtime Entity.create + Net.replicate(..., "Prefabs/…") Health / score / money / turn Net.broadcast + Net.on An action beyond WASD + fire Net.rpc(localPlayer, "action", data) → Net.onEntityRpc Categorical state without a packet encode it in the sprite path + Sync Sprite A per-player identity / color Net.playerSlot / Net.localEntity

docs.title: 7.7 Several scenes  -  lobby → level → results
docs.text:
The server decides which scene everyone plays. Call Scene.load on the server only; every client follows automatically.

-- lobby.lua (on any entity of Lobby.scene)
function Script:onUpdate(entity, dt)
    if Net.isServer() and everyoneReady() then
        Scene.load("levels/Level1.scene")
    end
end

What happens:

  1. At the end of that frame the server switches scenes and sends a reliable scene_load message to every client.
  2. Each client loads the same scene. Packets that arrive after scene_load wait until the client has switched, so nothing from the new scene lands in the old one.
  3. The server respawns every connected player in the new scene with the same network id and color slot (Net.playerSlot, Net.localEntity keep working).
  4. A client that joins later, or that was started on another scene, is moved to the server's current scene when it connects.

Rules of thumb:

  • Scene.load on a client is ignored (scripts often run on every machine).
  • Every machine needs the scene files: they ship in the same project folder.
  • Data that must survive a switch (scores, who is ready) lives in Lua globals on the server, then is sent again with Net.broadcast once the new scene starts. Handlers registered with Net.on stay registered; register them again in the new scene's onCreate if they use self.
  • Reloading the current scene (Scene.load(Scene.current())) works too: everyone reloads it.

docs.title: 8. Missing steps (not available yet)
docs.text: The multiplayer path is complete end to end for local playtests, but several conveniences are still missing. This list is the honest "what you cannot do yet".

docs.title: Playtest workflow
docs.text:
• Play Multiplayer does not build. If the game executable is missing or stale, the button does nothing (the processes fail to launch silently). Click 🔨 Build first.
  • Port and host are not in the UI. Clients always connect to 127.0.0.1:3000; changing that means editing main.cpp or launching from a terminal with --host / --port.
  • No per-client configuration. Every client gets identical arguments.

docs.title: Netcode & gameplay feel
docs.text:
• No client-side prediction. Input has at least one tick of latency, even on localhost. This is the biggest "feel" gap for fast games.
  • No interpolation. Remote entities move at the snapshot rate and can look steppy.
  • No lobby, matchmaking, server browser, password or authentication. You connect to a host and port; the server trusts the input it receives.
  • No reconnect / session resume. A dropped client is simply gone (its color slot is freed).
  • Hard cap of 5 players, baked into both the slot resource and the transport (a TODO to make it configurable).

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
• No in-editor play mode and no script execution in the editor (by design - scripts only run in the launched game).
  • No network inspector. There is no panel for peers, bandwidth, packet log or per-entity sync rates.
  • No simulated latency / jitter / packet loss for testing poor connections.
  • No hot reload. Code changes require a rebuild before the playtest reflects them.

docs.title: Design constraints (things to design around)
docs.text:
These are not bugs - they are the current shape of the system, and a game has to fit them.

  • One player prefab per scene. The engine keeps a single player prefab path (the first Client-authority template's Prefab Path in the current scene) and destroys every Client template when the scene loads, so every connection spawns that same prefab. A scene without a template keeps the previous scene's prefab. Two different player classes in one scene are not expressible today - give everyone the same prefab and vary look/behaviour per color slot (Net.playerSlot).
  • No private messages from Lua. Net.broadcast reaches everyone, and Lua cannot turn a player entity into its peer to Net.send to a single client. Anything a player must not see (a hidden hand, fog of war) cannot be withheld through the API - only by not sending it.
  • The input packet is a fixed 5-bit set (up/down/left/right/shoot). Any other button must go through an RPC (see §7.2); a sixth input bit is an engine change.
  • RPC direction is fixed. A client's RPC goes to the server only; the server's RPC goes to all clients.
  • Two client windows on one machine share one keyboard. Only the focused window receives key events, so you cannot drive two local clients at once by hand - use two machines, or the automated input hook (RTYPE_TEST_INPUT, see Engine → Diagnostics).

docs.title: Engine capabilities (TODOs)
docs.text:
• No prefab instantiation from Lua. Lua can only Entity.create() a bare entity; it cannot instantiate a .prefab. Players are spawned by the engine, not by Lua (see Engine → §14). Workaround: build the object on the server, then pass a prefabPath to Net.replicate so clients instantiate the authored prefab.
  • The 5-player cap is a compile-time constant. PlayerSlotState::kMaxPlayers is 5 and the transport refuses a 6th connection. Supporting a 6th player needs code changes (raise the constant and provide enough color/sprite blocks); making it a per-project setting is a TODO.

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause / fix Clicking Play Multiplayer does nothing The game executable is missing or stale - click 🔨 Build first. Client windows open but show a frozen scene The server failed to bind :3000 (already in use) or the client could not connect. Check the console logs. Only one player appears The scene entity is not Client authority, or its Prefab Path is empty (the server has nothing to spawn). All players look identical The color slot is not being read in your player script - use Net.playerSlot(entity) (see player.lua). Changes to scripts don't show up Rebuild the game, then relaunch; there is no hot reload. Need to see traffic Launch a process with RTYPE_NET_DEBUG=1 and watch its log for per-second input/position lines. A process lingers after Stop Stop kills each process group; if a child was launched outside it, kill it manually.

For the full protocol, packet reference and the Net API, see Engine → Networking & Multiplayer.

docs.title: Play mode
docs.text: The editor is an authoring tool: Lua does not run inside it, and the multiplayer plugin is not loaded into the editor process. Play and Play Multiplayer launch the real game binary with the current scene.

docs.title: Build
docs.text: Click the hammer to compile the project. The first build generates main.cpp and the CMake files if needed. Build output appears in the Console panel. Progress is shown on the button.

docs.title: Play
docs.text: Click the play triangle. The editor saves the scene first, then launches the executable with the current scene as an argument. If the executable is missing, build first.

docs.title: Play Multiplayer
docs.text:
Click the people icon. The editor saves the scene, then launches one server and N clients, each in its own window. Stop (which replaces the play buttons while games run) closes every launched process.

See Multiplayer for roles, settings, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The game starts on the scene being edited.
  • Script edits do not need a rebuild, but they do need a relaunch: save the file, close the game window, and click Play again.
  • There is no hot reload in the running process.

docs.title: Prefabs
docs.text: A prefab is a reusable entity subtree saved as a .prefab file. It is not a separate runtime concept: instantiating one copies the subtree and records the prefab path in a PrefabInstance component on the root.

docs.title: Creating a prefab
docs.text: Drag a Hierarchy row onto the Assets panel. Lucky writes <Name>.prefab in the folder you are viewing. If the name exists, the next file is Name_2.prefab, then Name_3.prefab.

docs.title: Instantiating
docs.text: Drag a .prefab from Assets onto the Hierarchy background (or a row) to instantiate it. The new subtree is a copy; positions are preserved per instance.

docs.title: Editing shared data
docs.text: Select a .prefab in Assets to open it in Preview. Changing the sprite path, scale, shape size, or script there updates every instance that still references it. Positions stay where each instance was placed, and a child position is applied as an offset from its parent.

docs.title: Runtime spawning
docs.text: The serializer installs a PrefabSpawner resource, so the engine can instantiate prefabs at runtime from C++ or from networked spawn messages. There is no Lua equivalent: a Lua script can only Entity.create() a bare entity and dress it with components.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Interface - Preview panel
  • Scenes
  • Networking - prefab spawning on clients

docs.title: Scenes
docs.text: A scene is a snapshot of the registry: entities, their components, and the project configuration. The editor writes it; the game reads it at startup.

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text:
Save with Ctrl+S or File → Save Scene. The file is written to m_ActiveScenePath. Save Scene As... writes to a new path and switches to it.

The game deserializes the same file at startup through Serialization::SceneSerializer. Deserialize returns false when the file cannot be read.

docs.title: Startup scene
docs.text:
Each project has a startup scene, named in project.json:

{"startupScene": "levels/Menu.scene"}

The game starts with that scene. In the editor, File → Set as Startup Scene marks the active scene. Projects without project.json default to test.scene.

docs.title: Scene files vs. prefabs
docs.text: .scene .prefab Scope Whole registry + config One entity subtree Edited in Scene view / Hierarchy Preview panel Instances One Many, sharing component data Reference - PrefabInstance on the root

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Scenes are human-readable JSON by default; SerializationFormat::Binary writes BEVE with the same snapshot structure. Asset paths are project-relative. See Reference → Scene format.

docs.title: New scene
docs.text: File → New Scene... creates an empty scene in the project folder. Scene switching inside the editor asks before discarding unsaved changes.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Interface
  • Prefabs
  • Command line
  • Scene format

docs.title: Shipping a game
docs.text: Shipping an editor-made game means producing a runnable executable that loads the scene you authored.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Click Build (hammer) in the editor, or build from the command line. The build writes main.cpp and a .editor_build.cmake, configures CMake with EDITOR_BUILD=ON, and compiles the executable named in the project settings (m_BuildExecutableName).

The executable is placed in the project folder, or in build/, build/<Config>/, or build/Games/R-Type/<Config>/ depending on the generator.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
The game takes the scene to start with as an argument:

./MyGame levels/Menu.scene

With no argument it uses the startup scene from project.json. Multiplayer roles come from flags:

./MyGame --server --headless
./MyGame --client --host 10.0.0.5 --port 4000

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: Bundled assets are compiled into the executable by AssetBundler, so a shipped game does not need its assets/ folder at runtime. Disk-loaded assets still need their files.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text: Ship the server and client binaries together, or run a dedicated server with --server --headless. See Multiplayer.

• Play mode

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
Use Pozzo as a C++ library: application loop, ECS, assets, rendering, audio, and networking.

  • Application - The main loop, window creation, and application lifecycle.
  • Building the engine - CMake targets, include paths, and linking.
  • Registry - Store entities and query their components.
  • Components - Define data and register component types.
  • Systems - Read and write component data every frame.
  • Resources - Share global services and state between systems.
  • Assets - Load, cache, and resolve textures, sounds, and data files.
  • Rendering - Sprites, text, cameras, and the render pipeline.
  • Input - Keyboard, mouse, and controller input.
  • Audio - Play sounds and music.
  • Collisions - Collision layers, detection, and response.
  • Networking - Synchronize state between clients and servers.
  • Lua scripting - Expose engine functionality to Lua.
  • Headless mode - Run the engine without a window.

docs.title: Application
docs.text: Engine::Application owns the window, the Registry, and the main loop. You create one in main(), register plugins, spawn entities, and call Run().

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Engine::ApplicationConfig is an aggregate with sensible defaults:

Field Default Notes windowWidth / windowHeight 1280 / 720 OS window size virtualWidth / virtualHeight 0 0 means "match the window", so the game runs 1:1 until you set a canvas size windowTitle "Game Engine" Window caption maximized false Adds the maximized window flag; the window is always resizable targetFPS 60 Fixed simulation step rate headless false No window, no rendering; systems and networking still tick args empty Command-line arguments; published as LaunchOptions and to Lua as arg onUI none Called after the canvas is presented; used by the editor for panels customRender none When set, the editor draws the registry into its own surface

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
Run() is a fixed-timestep loop:

while running:
    PreUpdate(dt)          input polling, virtual-canvas scaling, mouse mapping
    while lag >= step:
        Update(dt)         every registered system, in registration order
    PostUpdate(dt)         rendering: world pass, then screen pass
    FlushQueues()          deferred entity destruction
    ApplyPendingScene()     switch scenes requested during the frame

The step is 1.0 / targetFPS seconds. Gameplay multiplies by dt, so it is framerate-independent.

docs.title: Accessing the registry
docs.text:
Engine::Application app(config);
Engine::Registry& registry = app.GetRegistry();

The registry is created inside Application; components, systems, and resources are added through it. app.Quit() stops the loop from anywhere, including from a system.

docs.title: Headless mode
docs.text:
Set config.headless = true (or pass --headless to a generated game) to run without a window. InitWindow is skipped, VirtualResolution is not registered, and PostUpdate does nothing, but Update and PreUpdate still run. Networking and the SceneManager keep working, which is how the multiplayer server runs.

See Headless mode.

docs.title: Window and canvas
docs.text:
The OS window and the virtual canvas are separate. VirtualResolution scales a fixed-size render texture into the window with letterboxing or pillarboxing, and maps the mouse into canvas space. Set virtualWidth/virtualHeight to a fixed resolution (for example 1920x1080) to get a stable coordinate system regardless of window size.

See Rendering.

docs.title: Scene switching
docs.text: SceneManager is a resource that queues a scene change. ApplyPendingScene() runs after FlushQueues, so destruction from the previous scene is complete before the new one loads. Lua scripts use Scene.load(name); clients in multiplayer ignore their own request and follow the server.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text: Engine::AssetManager is a global resource that owns decoded sprites, sounds, music, and fonts. Components store ids and paths, not loaded objects; the manager turns ids into resources.

docs.title: Getting the manager
docs.text:
A plugin normally creates it (SpritePlugin and AudioPlugin both guard with HasResource):

auto& assets = registry.GetResource<Engine::AssetManager>();

If nothing has created it yet:

auto& assets = registry.AddResource<Engine::AssetManager>();

docs.title: Bundled assets
docs.text:
The AssetBundler compiles the project's assets/ folder into a generated header, so the executable ships with its assets and startup avoids disk I/O.

#include "BundledAssets.hpp"

auto& assets = registry.GetResource<Engine::AssetManager>();
BundledAssets::RegisterAssets(assets);

Ids are the relative file names under assets/ (player.png, laser.wav).

docs.title: Loading from disk
docs.text:
Useful for tools, mods, or very large optional packs:

assets.LoadSprite("player", "assets/player.png");
assets.LoadSound("explosion", "assets/boom.wav");
assets.LoadMusic("bgm", "assets/music.mp3", true); // true = loop

auto sprite = assets.GetSprite("player");   // throws ErrorAsset if missing
auto sound  = assets.GetSound("explosion");
auto music  = assets.GetMusic("bgm");

Unload explicitly when you are done with a large asset:

assets.UnloadSprite("player");
assets.UnloadSound("explosion");
assets.UnloadMusic("bgm");

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Asset paths in components are project-relative. The editor and the built game resolve them against the project folder, so the same .scene works in both. Do not store absolute paths in a component; they break on another machine and inside bundles.

Assets/ProjectPaths.hpp provides ResolveAssetPath, ResolveProjectPath, and ToProjectRelativePath for the cases where you need to convert.

docs.title: What lives where
docs.text:
Asset Loaded by Referenced from Sprites LoadSprite / bundler SpriteComponent.assetPath Sounds LoadSound / bundler AudioSource.assetId Music LoadMusic / bundler AudioSource.assetId Fonts LoadFontFromMemory Text.font

See also: Rendering · Audio · Text.

docs.title: Audio
docs.text: Audio is fully ECS-driven: gameplay sets fields on an AudioSource component and AudioSystem talks to the device. You never call Play() from gameplay code.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Engine::AudioPlugin audioPlugin;
audioPlugin.Init(app.GetRegistry());

That registers AssetManager (if missing), AudioSource, and AudioSystem, and opens the audio device.

docs.title: Loading audio
docs.text:
There are two asset kinds:

Kind Use for Behaviour Sound Lasers, hits, explosions Decoded into RAM, can overlap many times Music Background tracks Streamed from disk, one playhead per asset

From bundled assets (recommended):

#include "BundledAssets.hpp"

auto& assets = app.GetRegistry().GetResource<Engine::AssetManager>();
BundledAssets::RegisterAssets(assets);
if (assets.GetAllMusic().contains("music.mp3")) {
    assets.GetMusic("music.mp3").SetLooping(true);
}

From disk:

auto& assets = app.GetRegistry().GetResource<Engine::AssetManager>();
assets.LoadMusic("bgm_level1", "assets/music.mp3", true); // true = loop
assets.LoadSound("laser_pew", "assets/laser.wav");

Bundled ids are relative file names (laser.wav, not assets/laser.wav).

docs.title: Playing a sound
docs.text:
Attach the component and set shouldPlay. AudioSystem clears the flag when it has handled the request.

Engine::AudioSource audio;
audio.assetId = "laser_pew";
audio.isMusic = false;
audio.shouldPlay = true;
registry.AddComponent(laser, audio);

Or trigger from a gameplay system by flipping the field. This is the data-oriented pattern: gameplay mutates data, the audio system observes it.

docs.title: Background music
docs.text:
Engine::AudioSource bgm;
bgm.assetId = "bgm_level1";
bgm.isMusic = true;
bgm.shouldPlay = true;
registry.AddComponent(levelEntity, bgm);

Stop it with shouldStop = true. AudioSystem updates the streaming buffer every frame while a track plays.

docs.title: Overlapping sounds
docs.text: You do not manage voices. If 50 entities request laser_pew on the same frame, the asset manager hands out 50 lightweight aliases and AudioSystem mixes them, while keeping one decoded copy of the file in RAM. The alias list is pruned as sounds finish.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Nothing plays AudioPlugin::Init() was not called, or the device failed to open GetResource throws AudioPlugin was skipped and AssetManager was never registered Wrong asset id Bundled ids are relative paths Music restarts every frame shouldPlay is being set continuously instead of once Sound cut off The entity or its AudioSource was destroyed

docs.title: Building the engine
docs.text: Pozzo builds with CMake 3.28+ and C++23. Dependencies are fetched automatically by CPM on the first configure.

docs.title: Targets
docs.text: Target Type What it is Engine static library Core runtime, plugins, systems Serialization static library Scene and prefab serialization RTypeEditor executable The Lucky editor Game executable The R-Type game Server executable Headless multiplayer server Tests executable Engine tests

docs.title: Configure and build
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel

The first configure needs network access to download raylib, raylib-cpp, Dear ImGui, rlImGui, ENet, glaze, and sol2. They are cached in .cpm_cache/ and reused by later builds.

For development:

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
cmake --build build --target RTypeEditor --parallel

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Effect EDITOR_BUILD OFF Set by the editor when building a project; enables project-specific includes and scaffolded sources CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE - Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo

docs.title: Using the engine in your own project
docs.text:
Link Engine and Serialization and include their headers:

target_link_libraries(my_game PRIVATE Engine Serialization)
target_include_directories(my_game PRIVATE
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/Engine/include
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/Serialization/include
)

The engine requires C++23. Set CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23 in your project.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: CMake 3.28+, a C++23 compiler (GCC 13+, Clang 17+, MinGW-w64 GCC 13+), Git, pkg-config, and Lua 5.4 development headers. Linux needs the GL/X11/Wayland and audio libraries listed in Installation.
